Je vais déjeuner. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'allé').
Imperative used to encourage. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'allé').

examples.trans: I'm going to have lunch twice.

meanings.note: Afterwards or then, as an adverb.
After an event, as a preposition.

examples.text: Après, elles ne peuvent plus s'arrêter.
On mange, et après on part.
examples.trans: We eat, and afterwards we leave.

examples.text: Elles commencent avec un peu de Botox. Après, elles ne peuvent plus s'arrêter.
examples.trans: They start with a bit of Botox. Then they can't stop anymore.

meanings.note: No preposition: attendre quelqu'un. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to wait (for); to expect'.
Il vous attend?. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to wait (for); to expect'.

examples.text: Attendez-moi deux minutes devant le bureau!
examples.trans: Wait two minutes for me in front of the office!

examples.text: Nous attendons un appel très important de Los Angeles.
examples.trans: We are waiting for a very important call from Los Angeles.

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40

meanings.en: helper verb of the passé composé
meanings.note: J'ai appelé = I called. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.

meanings.en: il y a = there is, there are
meanings.note: Fixed expression. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.

examples.trans: We went back to my place.

meanings.note: D' before a vowel. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
le film de Tarantino = Tarantino's film
Also 'some': du sucre. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
The x sounds like z before a vowel. Spoken French num expression meaning 'two', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Deux places pour mardi? Mardi, tu as le film de Kechiche.
examples.trans: Two tickets for Tuesday? On Tuesday you've got the Kechiche film.

meanings.note: dire la vérité à quelqu'un = to tell someone the truth
dire à quelqu'un; dis-lui = tell her/him

meanings.note: Kiss someone; compound past uses avoir.
With se, kiss one another; compound past uses être.
Embrace or hug someone.

examples.trans: Love (at the end of a letter or call).

examples.text: L'envie subite de s'embrasser et de prendre une chambre? Ça arrive.

meanings.note: en retard = late, en vacances = on holiday

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

meanings.en: to come in, to go in

examples.trans: Come in, please, the door is open.

examples.text: Elle vient d'entrer dans le bureau de Mathias.

meanings.note: The t is never pronounced. French conjunction meaning 'and', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.

meanings.note: Until a time or event.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your valuable help today.

examples.text: Je te dis mille fois merci pour ce beau rôle!

meanings.note: Stressed form: pour moi, avec moi. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'me'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: C'est comme un rêve pour moi.
examples.trans: It's like a dream for me.

meanings.note: ma before a feminine noun, mon before a vowel

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.

meanings.note: at the end of a sentence: super, non?
Tag at the end of a question. Invariable French adverb meaning 'no'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

General. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'we'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: Exclamation of relief, phew.
Invariable French adverb meaning 'yes'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Oui, oui. J'ai juste besoin d'un petit cours.
examples.trans: Yes, yes. I just need a little lesson.

meanings.note: With ne, nobody or not anyone; it can be the subject or the object.
Une personne is the feminine noun for a person.

examples.text: Il ne laisse personne voir ses contrats.
examples.trans: He doesn't let anyone see his contracts.

meanings.note: With ne, no longer or no more.
More, a positive comparison; plus ou moins means more or less.

examples.trans: I can't take any more, Andréa.

meanings.note: For carrying an object.
For wearing clothing or an accessory.
In porter malheur or porter bonheur, bring bad or good luck.

examples.text: On n'offre pas du vert à une actrice. Ça porte malheur.
examples.trans: You don't give green to an actress. It brings bad luck.

meanings.note: Quelqu'un de jeune = someone young. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'someone'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Quelqu'un a dit à Cécile qu'elle était trop vieille pour le rôle.
